newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto reports record 1996 cargo traffic.
newsitem.headline: Toronto reports record 1996 cargo traffic.

text.p: Cargo traffic at Canada's largest airport increased 5.8 percent to a record 339,000 tonnes last year, up from 320,221 tonnes in 1995, the agency operating Toronto's Lester B. Pearson International Airport reported.

Passenger traffic rose eight percent, which unofficially made Pearson the 20th busiest airport in the world and the fourth busiest international airport in North America, the Greater Toronto Airport Authority said in a statement.

The single biggest factor for the traffic increases was a full year of operating under the Canada-U.S. Open Skies regime, which was introduced on Feb 23, 1995. U.S. carriers have been granted increased access to Toronto on a rationed basis, while Canadian carriers have been free to launch any route with some limitations on the number of flights per route.
All restrictions are eliminated next February.
